instruction: I have a presentation open in LibreOffice Impress and there's an image file called "slide_bg.png" on my Desktop that I extracted from it. Please open this image in GIMP, convert it to grayscale, and save it to the Desktop as "background.png". Thanks!

metadata.explanation: Task provides a pre-extracted image file (slide_bg.png) on Desktop. User opens this image in GIMP, converts it to grayscale, and saves as background.png. Evaluator checks if the saved image is in grayscale mode or has equal RGB channels. This makes the task fully verifiable - the evaluator can confirm the final image is grayscale and at the correct location.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Instruction states 'there is an image file called slide_bg.png on my Desktop that I extracted from it' (past tense) - the extraction has already been done. The actual task is to open slide_bg.png in GIMP, convert to grayscale, and save as background.png.
Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: (1) File exists at /home/user/Desktop/background.png, (2) File is in grayscale format.
Getter logic is correct: Downloads the image file from the specified path with proper error handling and file existence checks.
Metric logic is correct: Checks grayscale using comprehensive methods - native grayscale mode (L, LA) and RGB channel equality for converted images. Handles edge cases properly.
Parameter handling is correct: The metric function correctly accesses expected_state directly as the rules dict (no 'expected.get(rules)' errors).

No semantic gaps: The instruction does NOT require verifying the source of slide_bg.png or the extraction process - that has already happened. Only the GIMP processing (convert to grayscale and save) needs verification.
